title_ar: حكم بيع الطعام المستورد قبل وصوله مخازن التاجر | فتاوى الشيخ الددو
title_en: The Ruling on Selling Imported Food Before It Reaches the Merchant's Warehouses | Fatwas of Sheikh al-Dedew
body_ar:
سائل يسأل عن حكم بيع الطعام المستورد قبل وصوله مخازن التاجر وهل يدخل ضمن حرمة بيع الطعام قبل قبضه و على ذلك إذا باعه فارتفع سعره قبل وصوله فهل للبائع فسخ البيع أو رفع السعر .

عليكم السلام ورحمة الله وبركاته

بيع الطعام قبل وصوله إذا كان قد دخل في ملك البائع و ضمانه فكان مملوكا له ولم يعد مملوكا للشركة التي اشتراه منها، بأن كان هو الذي شحنه في البحر وهو الذي أمَّن عليه فإنه يجوز له بيعه لأنه أصبح في ملكه وحوزه ولو لم يصل إلى السوق ولو لم يصل إلى البلد أصلا ولو كان مشحونا في البحر وقبل أن يصل إلى الميناء يجوز له بيعه، وإذا باعه لا يحل له التراجع عن بيعه، لأن البيع قد مضى ولو ارتفع السعر بعد ذلك فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى يقول: { يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَوْفُوا بِالْعُقُودِ } و يقول : { وَالْمُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِهِمْ إِذَا عَاهَدُواْ } و يقول سبحانه وتعالى{ وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ إِذَا عَاهَدتُّمْ } وقد صح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: « آيَة المنافقِ ثلاث: إذا حَدَّث كَذَبَ، وإذا وعد أخلف، وإذا اؤتمن خان » رواه البخاري و صح عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : « أربع من كن فيه كان منافقا خالصا، ومن كانت فيه خصلة منهن كانت فيه خصلة من النفاق حتى يدعها: إذا اؤْتُمنَ خان، وإذا حدَّث كذب، وإذا عاهد غدر، وإذا خاصم فجر » رواه البخاري .

أجارنا الله و إياكم من النفاق و الشقاق و سوء الأخلاق و أغنانا و إياكم بحلاله عن حرامه.

و السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته

فتاوى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو الشنقيطي
body_en:
A questioner asks about the ruling on selling imported food before it reaches the merchant's warehouses, and whether this falls under the prohibition of selling food before taking possession of it (qabḍ); and, on that basis, if he sells it and its price rises before it arrives, whether the seller may rescind the sale or raise the price.

And upon you be peace, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

As to selling food before it arrives: if it has already entered the seller's ownership and his liability (ḍamān), so that it is owned by him and is no longer owned by the company from which he bought it — as where it was he who shipped it by sea and he who insured it — then it is permissible for him to sell it, because it has come into his ownership and his possession, even if it has not reached the market, even if it has not reached the country at all, and even if it is loaded on board at sea; before it reaches the port it is permissible for him to sell it. And once he has sold it, it is not lawful for him to go back on his sale, because the sale has already taken effect, even if the price rises afterwards. For God, glorified and exalted, says: { O you who believe, fulfil your contracts } (Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:1); and He says: { and those who fulfil their covenant when they make a covenant } (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:177); and the Glorified and Exalted says: { And fulfil the covenant of God when you have made a covenant } (Sūrat al-Naḥl 16:91). It is established as sound from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said: "The signs of the hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks his promise, and when he is entrusted he betrays the trust" — narrated by al-Bukhari. And it is established as sound from him (peace and blessings be upon him) that he said: "Four traits: whoever has them in him is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has in him a trait of hypocrisy until he abandons it — when he is entrusted he betrays the trust, when he speaks he lies, when he makes a covenant he acts treacherously, and when he disputes he behaves depravedly" — narrated by al-Bukhari.

May God protect us and you from hypocrisy, from discord and from bad character, and may He make what He has made lawful suffice us and you, so that we have no need of what He has forbidden.

And peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

Fatwas of His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew al-Shinqiti

flags.context: وهل يدخل ضمن حرمة بيع الطعام قبل قبضه
options: the prohibition of selling food before taking possession of it (qabḍ)
the forbiddenness of selling foodstuffs before receipt
the ban on reselling food before it is taken into possession
flags.note: قبض is the technical taking of possession that the hadith prohibition turns on; the schools differ on what constitutes it for goods in transit, and the Sheikh's answer here works entirely from ownership and ḍamān rather than from physical receipt. qabḍ is not in the glossary and should be added, since the whole fatwa turns on it.

flags.context: the second hadith, the fourth of the four traits
options: when he disputes he behaves depravedly
when he quarrels he resorts to foul play
when he disputes he transgresses all bounds
flags.note: فجر in this hadith denotes abandoning restraint in a dispute — lying, abusing, breaking the rules of the quarrel. 'Behaves depravedly' keeps the moral weight of the root; 'resorts to foul play' is more idiomatic English but narrower. The choice affects only tone, not the ruling.

options: The signs of the hypocrite are three
The mark of the hypocrite is threefold
The sign of the hypocrite is three things
flags.note: The Arabic has the singular آية with the numeral ثلاث; the standard English renders it as a plural. Kept as the conventional 'the signs ... are three'; the singular/plural mismatch is in the received wording of the report itself, not a CMS defect.

translator_notes: Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic (style guide section 4). Surah and verse references were identified by the translator; the source prints the verses without references.
A complete fatwa: question, ruling, evidence and closing supplication are all present, so it is typed fatwa and is not an excerpt.
يجوز له بيعه is rendered 'it is permissible for him to sell it'. The Sheikh gives permissibility, not encouragement, and the English has not been strengthened.

صح عن النبي is rendered 'it is established as sound from the Prophet': ṣaḥīḥ in its hadith-grading sense. The Sheikh's own attribution, 'narrated by al-Bukhari', is preserved exactly on both reports; no grading has been added and none dropped.
The hadith texts are set in guillemets in the source and in double quotation marks in the English, kept distinct from the curly braces reserved for Qur'anic quotation.
The three verses are printed in the source without references; the curly-brace format of style guide section 4 has been applied and the references were identified by the translator.
ضمان is rendered 'liability' here, the sense the glossary gives alongside 'guarantee': the point is that risk of loss has passed to the buyer, which is what makes the onward sale valid.
